fields.title: 📖 The Nuzūl of ʿĪsā ibn Maryam – refutation of the metaphorical reading
fields.body:
<!-- slide: 1 -->
# The Qurʾān: ʿĪsā was not killed

🖋️ Allah تعالى

“They neither killed him nor crucified him … rather, Allah raised him to Himself.”

The Qurʾān expressly denies his killing by his opponents and sets his being raised over against that.

📝 Qurʾān, an-Nisāʾ 4:157–158.

[→ Sources and direct references · Q35](/q/35/)

<!-- slide: 2 -->
# “Mutawaffīka” does not necessarily mean final death

🖋️ Allah تعالى

“Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those who have not died, during their sleep.”

🖋️ Allah تعالى

“And He is the One Who takes you by night.”

It is already clear from the Qurʾān: the verb tawaffā is not used exclusively for death.

Therefore the claim, “Mutawaffīka in Āl ʿImrān 3:55 can only mean that ʿĪsā has died finally,” is not linguistically compelling.

📝 Qurʾān, az-Zumar 39:42; al-Anʿām 6:60; Āl ʿImrān 3:55.

[→ Sources and direct references · Q35](/q/35/)

<!-- slide: 3 -->
# The real Ikhtilāf about Āl ʿImrān 3:55

The early Ikhtilāf must not be concealed.

🖋️ ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما

Through ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah it is transmitted from him about mutawaffīka:

“I cause you to die.”

This report exists and is not denied.

But it does not say: “ʿĪsā will never return.”
It does not say: “The Nuzūl is metaphorical.”
And it does not say: “A man born later from the Ummah is named ʿĪsā ibn Maryam in the Aḥādīṯ.”

📝 Aṭ-Ṭabarī, Ǧāmiʿ al-Bayān, Tafsīr of Āl ʿImrān 3:55.

[→ Sources and direct references · Q35](/q/35/)

<!-- slide: 4 -->
# Maṭar al-Warrāq and al-Ḥasan on mutawaffīka

🖋️ Maṭar al-Warrāq رحمه الله

“I take you out of this world; not by the taking of death.”

🖋️ Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī رحمه الله

“I take you from the earth.”

📝 Aṭ-Ṭabarī, Ǧāmiʿ al-Bayān, Tafsīr of Āl ʿImrān 3:55.

[→ Sources and direct references · Q35](/q/35/)

<!-- slide: 5 -->
# Ibn Zayd: Nuzūl before death

🖋️ Ibn Zayd رحمه الله

“Mutawaffīka means: I take you.”

Then he said about ʿĪsā:

“He has not yet died, until he kills the Daǧǧāl; after that he will die.”

Thus the order according to Ibn Zayd is:

He lives → he descends → he kills the Daǧǧāl → after that he dies.

📝 Aṭ-Ṭabarī, Ǧāmiʿ al-Bayān, Tafsīr of Āl ʿImrān 3:55.

[→ Sources and direct references · Q35](/q/35/)

<!-- slide: 6 -->
# Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī: “He is alive now”

🖋️ Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī رحمه الله

About an-Nisāʾ 4:159 he said:

“Before the death of ʿĪsā. By Allah, he is now alive with Allah; when he descends, they will all believe in him.”

From him it is also transmitted at the same place:

“ʿĪsā — and he has not yet died.”

This is not a later theological construction, but the statement of a great Tābiʿī.

📝 Aṭ-Ṭabarī, Ǧāmiʿ al-Bayān, Tafsīr of an-Nisāʾ 4:159.

[→ Sources and direct references · Q35](/q/35/)

<!-- slide: 7 -->
# Ibn ʿAbbās and the Nuzūl

🖋️ ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما

Concerning Allah’s statement:

“And indeed, he is a sign for the Hour”

it is transmitted from him:

“The descent of ʿĪsā ibn Maryam.”

This is decisive: even if the report from Ibn ʿAbbās, “mutawaffīka = I cause you to die,” is accepted, it does not follow that Ibn ʿAbbās denied the Nuzūl.

From him, precisely the descent of ʿĪsā ibn Maryam is transmitted.

📝 Aṭ-Ṭabarī, Ǧāmiʿ al-Bayān, Tafsīr of az-Zuḫruf 43:61.

[→ Sources and direct references · Q35](/q/35/)

<!-- slide: 8 -->
# Qatādah and Muǧāhid on az-Zuḫruf 43:61

🖋️ Qatādah رحمه الله

“The descent of ʿĪsā ibn Maryam is a sign for the Hour.”

🖋️ Muǧāhid رحمه الله

He explained the verse by the appearance of ʿĪsā ibn Maryam before the Day of Resurrection.

📝 Aṭ-Ṭabarī, Ǧāmiʿ al-Bayān, Tafsīr of az-Zuḫruf 43:61.

[→ Sources and direct references · Q35](/q/35/)

<!-- slide: 9 -->
# Aḍ-Ḍaḥḥāk on az-Zuḫruf 43:61

🖋️ Aḍ-Ḍaḥḥāk رحمه الله

He explained it by:

“the appearance of ʿĪsā ibn Maryam and his descent from heaven before the Day of Resurrection.”

📝 Aṭ-Ṭabarī, Ǧāmiʿ al-Bayān, Tafsīr of az-Zuḫruf 43:61.

[→ Sources and direct references · Q35](/q/35/)

<!-- slide: 10 -->
# The Prophet ﷺ says: “Ibn Maryam”

🖋️ The Messenger of Allah ﷺ

“How will it be with you when the son of Maryam descends among you and your Imām is from among you?”

The Prophet ﷺ did not say:

“a man like ʿĪsā,”
not: “a man with the title ʿĪsā,”
and not: “a Muslim born later who represents ʿĪsā.”

He said:

Ibn Maryam — the son of Maryam.

📝 Ṣaḥīḥ al-Buḫārī, no. 3449; Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, no. 155.

[→ Sources and direct references · Q35](/q/35/)

<!-- slide: 11 -->
# The Ummah, their Amīr, and ʿĪsā ibn Maryam

🖋️ The Messenger of Allah ﷺ

“A group of my Ummah will continue to fight for the truth …”

Then he said:

“Then ʿĪsā ibn Maryam descends.”

Thereupon their Amīr says to him:

“Come and lead the prayer for us.”

ʿĪsā declines.

The linguistic structure is clear:

my Ummah → their Amīr → then ʿĪsā ibn Maryam descends to them.

The text thus distinguishes between the Ummah that already exists, their leader, and ʿĪsā ibn Maryam.

This contradicts the claim that the announced ʿĪsā is merely a man born later from the same Ummah.

📝 Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, no. 156, from Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنه.

[→ Sources and direct references · Q35](/q/35/)

<!-- slide: 12 -->
# The just judge

🖋️ The Messenger of Allah ﷺ

“By the One in Whose hand is my soul: soon the son of Maryam will descend among you as a just judge. He will break the cross, kill the swine, and abolish the Ǧizyah.”

Again the same one is named expressly:

the son of Maryam.

📝 Ṣaḥīḥ al-Buḫārī, no. 3448; Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, no. 155.

[→ Sources and direct references · Q35](/q/35/)

<!-- slide: 13 -->
# Al-Masīḥ ibn Maryam — place, angels, and the Daǧǧāl

🖋️ The Messenger of Allah ﷺ

In the long Ḥadīṯ about the Daǧǧāl, the Prophet ﷺ reports that Allah will send:

al-Masīḥ ibn Maryam.

He descends at the white minaret east of Damascus.

His hands rest upon the wings of two angels.

Then he pursues the Daǧǧāl and kills him at the gate of Ludd.

The report names: al-Masīḥ ibn Maryam, a concrete place, angels, his Nuzūl, the Daǧǧāl, his pursuit, and his killing at Ludd.

The text itself gives no indication that “al-Masīḥ ibn Maryam” means another person born later.

📝 Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, no. 2937, from an-Nawwās ibn Samʿān رضي الله عنه.

[→ Sources and direct references · Q35](/q/35/)

<!-- slide: 14 -->
# Imām aṭ-Ṭabarī — d. 310 H.

🖋️ Imām aṭ-Ṭabarī رحمه الله

After mentioning the differing interpretations of mutawaffīka, he prefers the meaning:

“I take you from the earth and raise you to Me.”

As his reason he cites the reports, transmitted through many routes, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that ʿĪsā ibn Maryam will:

descend and kill the Daǧǧāl,
then remain for a time upon the earth,
and afterwards die.

Thus it already stands firm in 310 H.: the Ikhtilāf about tawaffī was known to aṭ-Ṭabarī. Nevertheless he understood the numerous reports of the Nuzūl as proof of the future personal Nuzūl of ʿĪsā ibn Maryam.

📝 Aṭ-Ṭabarī, Ǧāmiʿ al-Bayān, Tafsīr of Āl ʿImrān 3:55.

[→ Sources and direct references · Q35](/q/35/)

<!-- slide: 15 -->
# Aṭ-Ṭaḥāwī — d. 321 H.

🖋️ Abū Ǧaʿfar aṭ-Ṭaḥāwī

“We believe in the signs of the Hour: in the appearance of the Daǧǧāl and in the descent of ʿĪsā ibn Maryam from heaven.”

Here it stands expressly:

ʿĪsā ibn Maryam → from heaven.

📝 Aṭ-Ṭaḥāwī, al-ʿAqīdah aṭ-Ṭaḥāwiyyah, section on the signs of the Hour.

[→ Sources and direct references · Q35](/q/35/)

<!-- slide: 16 -->
# Ibn Baṭṭah — d. 387 H.

🖋️ Imām Ibn Baṭṭah al-ʿUkbarī رحمه الله

In his presentation of the foundations upon which, according to his statement, Ahl al-Islām and the Ummah had agreed, Ibn Baṭṭah expressly mentions:

“Then the belief that ʿĪsā ibn Maryam descends from heaven to the earth, breaks the cross, and kills the swine.”

This is an early witness to consensus from the 4th century.

📝 Ibn Baṭṭah, aš-Šarḥ wa-l-Ibānah / al-Ibānah aṣ-Ṣuġrā, pp. 191 and 241 of the edition consulted.

[→ Sources and direct references · Q35](/q/35/)

<!-- slide: 17 -->
# Abū ʿAmr ad-Dānī — d. 444 H.

🖋️ Imām Abū ʿAmr ad-Dānī رحمه الله

He counts among that which must be believed on the basis of the authentic transmission from the Prophet ﷺ:

“The descent of ʿĪsā.”

He also mentions the breaking of the cross and the killing of the Daǧǧāl.

About an-Nisāʾ 4:159 he explains:

“Before the death of ʿĪsā, when he descends.”

Thus this article of belief is also expressly documented in 444 H.

📝 Abū ʿAmr ad-Dānī, ar-Risālah al-Wāfiyah li-maḏhab Ahl as-Sunnah, nos. 168–169, p. 243.

[→ Sources and direct references · Q35](/q/35/)

<!-- slide: 18 -->
# The decisive difference

It is factually correct to say:

Among the early Mufassirūn there was Ikhtilāf about the meaning and the temporal placing of tawaffī.

But from this it does not follow:

That among the Salaf there was Ikhtilāf about whether the authentic Nuzūl-Aḥādīṯ meant another man, born later, from the Ummah.

These are two different questions.

📝 Summary of the documented Tafsīr-Ikhtilāf and the Nuzūl-Aḥādīṯ; original references /q/35/.

[→ Sources and direct references · Q35](/q/35/)

<!-- slide: 19 -->
# Whom the early sources actually name

The early sources speak of:

ʿĪsā ibn Maryam.
Al-Masīḥ ibn Maryam.
The son of Maryam.
His descent from heaven.
His meeting the Ummah that already exists.
The Amīr of this Ummah, already present.
His killing of the Daǧǧāl.
And his later death.

For the claim:

“The announced ʿĪsā ibn Maryam is merely another human being, born later in the Ummah, and called ʿĪsā only metaphorically”

no corresponding proof from the Ṣaḥābah, the Tābiʿīn, or the named Imāms up to the 5th century is found in these early texts.

📝 Ṣaḥīḥ al-Buḫārī 3448–3449; Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 155–156, 2937; aṭ-Ṭabarī on 3:55 and 43:61; aṭ-Ṭaḥāwī; Ibn Baṭṭah; ad-Dānī.

[→ Sources and direct references · Q35](/q/35/)

<!-- slide: 20 -->
# Conclusion: the personal Nuzūl

The early Ikhtilāf about mutawaffīka is real and must not be concealed. It does not, however, concern the identity of the ʿĪsā ibn Maryam named in the authentic Nuzūl-Aḥādīṯ.

The Sunnah expressly distinguishes between the Ummah, their Amīr, and ʿĪsā ibn Maryam, who descends to them.

The early texts of Tafsīr and ʿAqīdah confirm the same personal Nuzūl.

A later metaphorical substitute person is not named in these early sources.

📝 Overall conclusion from the Qurʾān, the authentic Sunnah, and the early texts of Tafsīr and ʿAqīdah; direct references /q/35/.

[→ Sources and direct references · Q35](/q/35/)
